idiom_name: Slick TableQuery as the collection-like query surface, wrapped by a thin repository class
implementation_notes: Slick's TableQuery[Invoices] behaves like a Scala collection - map, filter, sortBy, join build a query that db.run(q.result) executes as a Future or DBIOAction - so the collection-like interface is provided by the library and the repository is a thin class holding the Database and exposing domain-language methods. Composition replaces the hand-written mapper, DBIO supplies the unit-of-work building block (DBIO.sequence composed with transactionally), and tests substitute an in-memory H2 database or a repository trait. The classic hand-written structure is only justified for stores or query shapes Slick cannot express, where plain JDBC or a query library takes over behind the same interface.
pitfalls: Slick's filter/sortBy are SQL: returning a Query from the repository pushes query building back to callers and makes accidental N+1 loading easy - return materialised results, and use join/prefetch deliberately.
db.run schedules work on Slick's execution context; an unconfigured AsyncExecutor or oversized queue starves the connection pool under load while looking asynchronous.
+= and result are DBIO actions, not side effects: group them with DBIO.sequence(...).transactionally to get one transaction, otherwise each action commits separately.
